To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
curl-up exercises in the position of upper and lower limb extension result in the highest RA and RF activity and in the lowest ES activity.
changing the position and movement of the extremities in curl-up exercises results in different muscle activity and different muscular loads in abdominal exercises.
curl-up exercises are performed with different muscle loads, depending on the position in the upper and lower limbs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the EMG activity during curl-up exercises with various positions of the upper extremities (extended behind the head, extended along the trunk, or flexed at 180° in the shoulder joint) and various positions of the lower extremity (flexed at 90 or 180° in hip and knee joints).
the biomechanical analysis of curl-up exercises with various positions of the upper extremities and the lower extremity.
the effect of the position of upper and lower limbs on the intensity of the EMG activity in curl-up abdominal strength exercises.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

curl-up exercises performed with the upper extremity extended along the trunk or extended behind the head with the lower extremity extended at 90° or flexed at 45° in the hip joint and at 90° and 0° in the knee joint are the most appropriate exercises for the RA.
curl-up exercises should be performed with the lower extremities extended at 90° at the hip and knee, and with the upper extremity extended along the trunk.
the EMG activity in the RA and ES is affected by different positions of the upper extremities and the position of the lower limbs in curl-up exercises.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
curl-up exercise with the upper extremity extended behind the head with the lower extremity flexed at 45° in the hip joints and at 90° knee joints involves the greatest RA activity.
changing the position and load of upper and lower limbs during curl-up exercises affects the EMGs of the RA and ES.
curl-up exercises performed with different positions of the upper extremities and with the lower extremities extended in the hip and flexed in the knee joints are recommended for the training of RA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the position of upper and lower limbs in curl-up exercises affects the EMGs of RA and ES, but not RF.
curl-up exercises are characterized by a different level of muscular activity in RA depending on the position adopted by the extremities.
curl-up exercise with upper extremities extended in front of the trunk and lower extremities flexion at the knee joints should be avoided because it involves the highest level of EMG activity of ES.
